page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What a zoo is
steps.why: A zoo keeps the animal alive and in one place, and that is what makes it useful for study — a preserved specimen cannot be watched feeding or behaving.
common_mistakes: Describing a zoo as a museum. A museum holds dead preserved specimens; a zoo holds living animals.
Writing only about entertainment. The question asks about study and classification.
steps.memory_tip: A zoo holds animals alive; a museum holds them preserved.
steps.margin_note: One sentence on what a zoo is. Two lines are enough.

steps.label: How it helps classification
steps.why: Classification is done on characters, and a zoo is the one place where the characters of a living animal — how it looks, what it eats, how it behaves — can be recorded directly.
common_mistakes: Naming only the external characters. Feeding habits and behaviour are studied as well, and they carry the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Three things a zoo lets you record: what the animal looks like, what it eats, how it behaves.
